turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from Device Physics

**Architecture recap (p-i-n / inverted):** Light enters through the transparent substrate → HTL → MAPbI₃ → ETL → back contact. Efficiency in this system is dominated by:

1. **ETL selectivity & interface passivation** (fullerene + a good buffer like BCP/Bphen that blocks holes and manages the top contact).
2. **HTL quality on the substrate** — the best inverted MAPbI₃ cells use either optimized **PTAA** (with passivation) or optimized **NiO-c** (especially with dopants/SAMs), or well-engineered PEDOT:PSS.
3. **Back contact chemistry** — Cu and Au give clean, stable contacts to fullerene/BCP; Ag works but is more prone to halide reactions.
4. **Substrate** — rigid SLG|ITO/FTO outperforms flexible PET/PEN/textile (lower sheet resistance, better film quality).

## Screening the training data for the top-performing motifs

Looking at the highest-target rows (>18%), the recurring winning ingredients are:
- **PTAA HTL with Cu back contact** (`C60|BCP,PTAA,Cu` → 18.62, 18.85, 19.085) — extremely reproducible high performers.
- **NiO-c HTL with dopant/SAM engineering** (`[BMIM]BF4`, `SDBS`, `Au-np|NiO`, `SY4`, `NiO-c|PTAA`) → 17.4–21.3.
- **C60|BCP with NiO-np** (Choline chloride treated → 19.7; plain → 17.8).
- Clean fullerene/BCP + PTAA generally lands 16–19%.

Low performers: bare PEDOT:PSS without buffer, flexible substrates, exotic/unknown organics, Al contacts on fullerene (worse than Cu/Au/Ag+buffer).

## Evaluating strong pool candidates

- **c044** `C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu` — *exact match* to the 18.6–19.1% training champions. Ideal fullerene/BCP stack + PTAA + Cu. **Top pick.**
- **c085** `TTC|C60|BCP, PTAA, Ag` — passivating small-molecule (TTC) + C60/BCP + PTAA. Mirrors the ~17.4% C60/BCP+SAM+PTAA family, with extra passivation.
- **c009** `C60|BCP, NiO-c, Ag` — clean C60/BCP with NiO-c; training shows this family at 14.6–18% and NiO-c is a top HTL here.
- **c041** `PCBM-60|BCP, NiMgLiO-c, Ag` — Li/Mg-doped NiO is the doped-NiO family that gave 18.2% (`NiMgLiO-c`) in training. Doped NiO = high conductivity + good band alignment.
- **c035** `TEAI|PCBM-60|PEI, NiO-c, Ag` — TEAI + PEI dual interface passivation on NiO-c; the `TEACl|PCBM|PEI/NiO-c` analog gave 15.3%, and interface passivation reliably pushes NiO-c cells up.

c044 and c085 (PTAA+fullerene) and the doped/engineered-NiO candidates are the physically strongest, most-reproducible recipes.

**Final: c044, c085, c041, c009, c035**
